The github above has my first attempt at shiny, at summarizing results of AB testing with a few tables and graphs. The code has been lifted from a working R script and dropped into the relevant places in server.R. However, it is now throwing errors saying that it can't find an object, even though a quick debug to std err() shows that there is a value for the objects in question..

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 code throwing errors when used in shiny, when error free in a regular script
parts:
The way that ggplot2 evaluates arguments in aes() is a little unusual
(it tries to evaluate them in the environment where you called
ggplot()). In your case, it seems that expressions within aes() aren't
able to access the variables in the parent environment, but they are
able to access the columns in the data frame passed to ggplot(). It's
possible that Shiny is not getting the environments quite right. I'll
take a look into that.

To work around this issue, one thing you can do for the vlines is to
take the xintercept out of aes(). So instead of this:
geom_vline(aes(xintercept=e), color="red", linetype="dashed")
You have this:
geom_vline(xintercept=e, color="red", linetype="dashed")


As for the layers where you have the aesthetic mapping depend on the value of x:
layer(data = d, mapping = aes(x=ifelse(x > e,x,e), y=y), geom = "area",
geom_params=list(fill="#00A5FF",alpha=.3))

This is a bit unusual - if I understand it correctly, you want to
compare the values in the column d$x to the single number stored in
the variable e; for each row, use the larger of the two values. You
could work around this by creating a new column in d, called xe, with
something like this:
d$xe <- ifelse(x > e, x, e)

Then use aes(x = xe, y=y).


-Winston

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 code throwing errors when used in shiny, when error free in a regular script
parts:
I think I've figured it out. The issue is with ggplot, not shiny. If
you take a look at ggplot.data.frame, you'll see that it defaults to
use the global environment for evaluating the aes() stuff:

> ggplot2:::ggplot.data.frame
function (data, mapping = aes(), ..., environment = globalenv())
...


The solution is to specify ggplot(environment=environment()), so that
it evaluates the stuff from aes() inside of the calling environment,
instead of inside the global environment.

So instead of this:
plot.2 <- ggplot(data = d, mapping = aes(x = x, y = y)) +
You would have this:
plot.2 <- ggplot(data = d, mapping = aes(x = x, y = y), environment
= environment())

I've put the code at:
https://gist.github.com/4349072


I'll have to talk to Hadley about whether the global environment thing
is a bug or feature in ggplot2.


-Winston

Thanks Winston, that did the trick.

As to what I am doing: I am showing the normal distribution curves associated with the Control and winning Test Cell, and shading the area that equates to the percentage of time that a random sample being given the Test Cell treatment (free vertical), 'will' perform better than the control group mean (blue vertical), plus some arbitrary desired lift (red vertical).

Still very much a work in progress.
